title: Workflow Lifecycle, Extension, and Recovery
readerIntent: Design and operate a durable workflow safely.
priorKnowledge: Know the business states, actors, items, decisions, and side effects.
owner: Workflow definitions, durable carriers/items, action/channel services, and target capabilities
summary: Definitions select a head action; commands or events create tenant-scoped carriers; transitions persist before continuation; restart recovers from durable state.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
items: Release begins automatic work or exposes a permitted manual action.
Action result selects an allowed channel and persists the transition.
Splits create traceable branches; aggregation waits under explicit policy.
Pause, resume, block, retry, cancel, finish, archive, and error states remain durable.

sections.heading: Extension
items: Project modules add definitions, mappings, actions, channels, handlers, interceptors, pipelines, events, validation, and access policy.
Runtime workflow-builder data must use the same governed definitions and cannot accept arbitrary executable code.
External API and AI actions use adapters, secrets, token/cost policy, timeouts, idempotency, audit, and human approval where risk requires.

sections.heading: Recovery proof
items: Duplicate/out-of-order events, concurrency, restart, remote timeout, late response, retry/replay, split/aggregation, definition versions, cancellation, compensation, redaction, performance, integration, and regression.
